_meta.indication: Tekturna (aliskiren) is indicated for the treatment of hypertension; may be used alone or in combination with other antihypertensive agents.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Five pivotal randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled 8-week antihypertensive trials (Studies 1201, 2201, 2203, 2204, 2308)
pivotal_trials.phase: Antihypertensive efficacy trials (phase not stated in the review)
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials of eight weeks' duration
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in seated trough cuff diastolic blood pressure (DBP) at eight weeks, with SBP as a secondary endpoint
pivotal_trials.n: Median group n per study ranged from 114 to 185 across the five pivotal studies
pivotal_trials.result: Aliskiren reduced blood pressure; placebo-subtracted seated trough DBP reductions were statistically significant (p<0.05 vs placebo) in the pivotal studies, e.g. -7.4 (Study 1201), -5.2 (Study 2201), -7.6 (Study 2308).

key_safety: Most common AE is dose-related diarrhea (2.3% at 300 mg vs 1.2% placebo); other increased events were rash (1% vs 0.3%), elevated uric acid (0.4% vs 0.1%), gout (0.2% vs 0.1%), and renal stones (0.2% vs 0%). Serious risks include angioedema (two cases with respiratory symptoms; rate 0.06%) and hypotension.
target_moa: Aliskiren is an orally active, nonpeptide, direct renin inhibitor. It inhibits renin, the enzyme that cleaves angiotensinogen to angiotensin I, thereby reducing plasma renin activity (PRA), Ang I and Ang II.
modality: Small molecule (orally active, nonpeptide renin inhibitor), aliskiren hemifumarate

boxed_warning.content: Use in pregnancy warning: when used during the second and third trimesters, drugs that act directly on the renin-angiotensin system can cause injury and even death to the developing fetus; discontinue Tekturna as soon as pregnancy is detected.

basis.text: Review division assigned a Priority Designation of S (Standard review), not priority.

summary.text: Tekturna (aliskiren), an oral direct renin inhibitor and the first renin inhibitor submitted for approval, was submitted as a 505(b)(1) NDA received February 13, 2006, given a Standard review designation, and approved March 5, 2007 for the treatment of hypertension based on five pivotal randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials with a primary endpoint of change in seated trough cuff DBP; a PREA pediatric study was deferred as a postmarketing requirement.

citations.quote: submitted under section 505(b)(1) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act for Tekturna (aliskiren) 150 mg and 300 mg Tablets.
This new drug application provides for the use of Tekturna (aliskiren) 150 mg and 300 mg Tablets for the treatment of hypertension.
Aliskiren is the first renin inhibitor submitted for approval. Aliskiren is the first renin inhibitor submitted for approval. It is formulated as film-coated tablets for oral administration.
a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of eight week's duration with a primary endpoint of change from baseline in seated trough cuff diastolic blood pressure (DBP).

requirement.text: Include intestinal procedures/neoplasms and angioedema as events of special interest in the proposed ALTITUDE outcome trial and provide periodic safety summaries.

citations.quote: To include intestinal procedures and neoplasms and angioidema as events of special interest in your proposed ALTITUDE trial as detailed in their special protocol assessment letters.

requirement.text: Incorporate a colonoscopy substudy (colonoscopies at baseline and after >=12 months treatment) into the proposed long-term outcome study, powered to rule out a doubling in cancerous/precancerous lesions.

citations.quote: To incorporate a colonoscopy substudy into your proposed long-term outcome study. The colonoscopy substudy should include colonoscopies performed at baseline and after drug treatment for 12 months or longer. This study should be powered to rule out a doubling in the rate of cancerous or precancerous lesions.

requirement.text: Provide evidence regarding the clinical usefulness (or lack thereof) of twice-daily dosing in patients not controlled on the highest recommended once-daily dose.

citations.quote: You should provide evidence that it is not likely to be clinically useful to give aliskiren in a twice-daily dosing regimen to patients whose blood pressure is not controlled on the highest recommended dose given once daily.
